info.title: Ambivo Unified Model Endpoint
info.description:
The `/entity/data` endpoint is a consolidated interface for querying, exporting,
and updating entity data across all standard entity types. It replaces
individual legacy endpoints (e.g., `/user/lead/manage_contacts`, `/user/order/manage`)
with a single, consistent API surface.

## Recommended Usage

This endpoint is designed primarily for **read and update** operations:

| Operation | Recommended? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GET** (query, list) | **Yes** | Primary use case |
| **Export** (CSV, JSON) | **Yes** | Up to 5000 records |
| **Aggregate** (charts) | **Yes** | Group-by queries for reporting |
| **Picklist** (dropdowns) | **Yes** | Dropdown population with tenant_scope |
| **Batch Retrieval** (get_entity_ids) | **Yes** | Fetch specific records by ID |
| **PATCH** (bulk update) | **Yes** | Primarily for bulk `$set` updates across multiple records |
| **PATCH** (single record) | Supported | Single-record partial update with deep merge on custom_form_dict |
| **DELETE** | Use with caution | Service-based entities have cascading deletes |
| **CREATE** | **Not recommended** | Use legacy entity-specific endpoints instead |

> **Why not CREATE?** Creating entities triggers cascading workflows — generating
> activities, updating linked records, creating comments, and managing attachments.
> These side effects are handled by the individual entity endpoints
> (e.g., `/user/lead/manage_contacts` with `action=add`). Using `/entity/data`
> for creation would bypass those workflows.

## Authentication
All requests require a Bearer JWT token in the `Authorization` header.

## Response Pattern
All JSON responses follow this convention:
- **Success**: `{ "result": 1, "data": {...}, "msg_list": [...] }`
- **Error**: `{ "result": 2, "error": "error_code", "message": "details" }`

## Supported Entity Types

33 types, read from `_supported_entities` in `MdReqHandler`. Anything else is refused.

**Collection** is what the records are stored in, and it is not always the entity_type with
underscores: `lead` is `leadcontacts`, `contact` is `accountcontacts`, `task` is `user_tasks`.
**Native key** is the key the records come back under when `use_native` is true; `legacy` means the
entity has no `to_native_response`, so the records arrive under `values` (see Serialization below).

| entity_type | Collection | Native key | Has userid? | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | `accounts` | `accounts` | Yes | |
| `attendance_day` | `attendance_day` | `attendance_day` | Yes | |
| `bill` | `bill` | `bill` | Yes | |
| `contact` | `accountcontacts` | `account_contacts` | Yes | |
| `custom_status` | `custom_status` | `custom_status` | No | tenant-wide |
| `file` | `stored_files` | `files` | Yes | |
| `folder` | `file_folders` | `folders` | Yes | |
| `goods_receipt` | `goods_receipt` | `goods_receipt` | Yes | |
| `installed_base` | `installed_base` | `legacy` | Yes | |
| `inventory_count_line` | `inventory_count_line` | `inventory_count_line` | Yes | |
| `inventory_count_session` | `inventory_count_session` | `inventory_count_session` | Yes | |
| `inventory_forecast` | `inventory_forecast` | `inventory_forecast` | Yes | |
| `inventory_item` | `inventory_item` | `inventory_item` | Yes | |
| `inventory_lot` | `inventory_lot` | `inventory_lot` | Yes | |
| `inventory_txn` | `inventory_txn` | `inventory_txn` | Yes | |
| `invoice` | `invoice` | `invoice` | Yes | |
| `lead` | `leadcontacts` | `lead_contacts` | Yes | |
| `marketing_source` | `marketing_sources` | `marketing_sources` | No | tenant-wide |
| `opportunity` | `opportunity` | `opportunities` | Yes | |
| `order` | `order` | `order` | Yes | |
| `payment` | `payment` | `legacy` | Yes | |
| `plaid_item` | `plaid_item` | `legacy` | Yes | |
| `product` | `product_item` | `product` | Yes | |
| `punch_event` | `punch_event` | `punch_event` | Yes | |
| `purchase_order` | `purchase_order` | `legacy` | Yes | |
| `purchase_requisition` | `purchase_requisition` | `purchase_requisition` | Yes | |
| `purchase_requisition_line` | `purchase_requisition_line` | `purchase_requisition_line` | Yes | |
| `shift_assignment` | `shift_assignment` | `shift_assignment` | Yes | |
| `shift_change_request` | `shift_change_request` | `shift_change_request` | Yes | |
| `task` | `user_tasks` | `tasks` | Yes | |
| `vendor` | `accounts` | `accounts` | Yes | alias: an `account` with `relationship_type` pinned to `vendor` |
| `vendor_price_agreement` | `vendor_price_agreement` | `vendor_price_agreement` | Yes | |
| `work_shift` | `work_shift` | `work_shift` | Yes | |

### Aliases

`vendor` is not a collection. It resolves to `account` with `relationship_type: "vendor"` pinned into
`match_filter_dict`, **overwriting** whatever the caller sent for that key. So asking for a vendor
never returns a customer, however the filter is written.

## Serialization — `use_native` Parameter

Controls how records are serialized in responses. **Default: `true`**.

**Resolution:** `_use_native = use_native AND hasattr(entity, 'to_native_response')`

| use_native | has to_native_response | Action | Serializer | Collection Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `true` | `true` | any | `to_native_response()` | Entity-specific (e.g. `"leads"`) |
| `true` | `false` | export, picklist | `toJSONExport()` | `"values"` |
| `true` | `false` | get, get_entity_ids | `toJSON()` | `"values"` |
| `false` | any | export, picklist | `toJSONExport()` | `"values"` |
| `false` | any | get, get_entity_ids | `toJSON()` | `"values"` |

**Key terminology:**
- **Native** (`use_native: true`) = **new** serializer, entity-specific collection key
- **Legacy** (`use_native: false`) = **old** `toJSON()` serializer, generic `"values"` key

## Access Control — `tenant_scope` Parameter

By default, queries are filtered by the requesting user's access permissions
(userid + role hierarchy).

| User Type | tenant_scope=true |
|---|---|
| Tenant admin | Allowed for **all** actions — bypasses userid filter |
| Non-admin | Allowed **only** for `action=picklist` (dropdown population) |
| Entity without userid | Auto-enabled — always queries tenant-wide |

For entity types without a `userid` field (e.g., `marketing_source`, `custom_status`),
`tenant_scope` is automatically set to `true` regardless of the request.

## Inventory and procurement picklists

For `inventory_item`, `inventory_txn`, `inventory_lot`, `inventory_count_session`, `inventory_count_line`, `inventory_forecast`, `purchase_order`, `purchase_requisition`, `vendor_price_agreement` and `goods_receipt`,
`action=picklist` is read through the entity's own service. The response
shape is the same as any picklist. The differences:

- The caller needs `R` on the module (`purchase_order` for orders). Without
  it the answer is `result: 2` with the service's `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_<MODULE>`
  code and the message "You cannot view this list."
- `tenant_scope` is ignored. The service decides what the caller sees.
- `page_size` defaults to 1000 and is at most 1000.
- A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED` (inventory types) or
  `PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED` (procurement types), never an empty list.
- To look up rows by id, send `match_filter_dict={"_id": {"$in": [...]}}`.
  Each id is a bare 24-character hex id or `"ObjectId('<hex id>')"`. `id`
  and `<entity_type>_id` are read as `_id`.

Each row carries `name` and `<entity_type>_id`. `name` joins these parts with
` · ` and skips blank ones:

| entity_type | `name` is built from |
|---|---|
| `inventory_item` | product name (or SKU), `site_code`, `location_code`, `bin_code` |
| `inventory_txn` | product name, `txn_type`, `qty`, `uom` |
| `inventory_lot` | `lot_number`, product name, `expiry_date` |
| `inventory_count_session` | name (or code), `count_date` |
| `inventory_count_line` | product name, `location_code`, session name |
| `inventory_forecast` | product name (or SKU), `site_code`, `period_key` |
| `purchase_requisition` | `requisition_number`, `name` |
| `vendor_price_agreement` | `agreement_number` (or `name`), product name (or SKU) |
| `goods_receipt` | `receipt_number`, `po_number`, `receipt_date` |
| `purchase_order` | the order's own `name` (rows always under `values`) |

## Fixed-list picklists

These entity types have no records behind them. They answer GET
`action=picklist` only, and need no `tenant_scope`. The rows are under
`data.values`: `{"result": 1, "data": {"values": [...], "total_count": N},
"gross_count": N}`.

| entity_type | `match_filter_dict` keys | Row fields |
|---|---|---|
| `inventory_uom` | `dimension` (`count`, `weight`, `volume`, `length`) | `code`, `label`, `dimension`, `precision`, `is_pack` |
| `inventory_item_type` | none | `code`, `label`, `description`, `example`, `dimensions` |
| `inventory_txn_type` | `hand_entry` (bool) | `code`, `label`, `description`, `action`, `source_type`, `inbound`, `signed_by_caller`, `reason_required`, `moves_to_another_place` |
| `inventory_txn_source_type` | none | `code`, `label`, `books_owns_it` |
| `inventory_txn_reason` | `txn_action`, `txn_type_code` | `code`, `label`, `is_waste` |
| `site` | `include_inactive` (bool) | `code`, `name`, `is_primary`, `is_active` |

`site` returns inactive sites too, unless `include_inactive` is `false`. Its
`data` also carries `codes_enforced`. It is false when the tenant has no
registered sites, and then any site code is accepted.

Any other action on a fixed list, GET or POST, answers `result: 2`,
`error_code: INVALID_DATA`, message "This list supports action=picklist only".
POST with `action=picklist` answers the same code with the message "Use GET
for this list. It supports action=picklist only".

## Filters that are refused

On GET and POST, a `match_filter_dict` that contains `$where`, `$function` or
`$accumulator` at any depth answers `result: 2`, `error_code: INVALID_DATA`,
message "This filter is not allowed." `$expr` is allowed.

## Pagination

All list queries support offset-based pagination:
- `page_size` — records per page (default varies; export capped at 5000)
- `page_num` — page number (1-indexed)
- `get_count` — return only count, no data (`true`/`false`)
- `sort_dict` — JSON sort object (e.g. `{"_id": -1}`)
- `match_filter_dict` — JSON filter object (e.g. `{"status": "active"}`)
- `search_text` — full-text search across searchable fields

## Filter Key Normalization
The endpoint automatically normalizes common filter key aliases:
- `created_ts` is mapped to `timestamp` for entities that use `timestamp` internally

## Important Limitations
- **Do NOT use this endpoint for CREATE operations.** Create has cascading impacts
  on related entities (activities, comments, attachments) handled by legacy endpoints.
  Use the individual entity endpoints (e.g., `/user/lead/manage_contacts` with `action=add`).
- **DELETE with caution.** While DELETE is supported, the legacy entity endpoints
  handle cascading cleanup more thoroughly.
- **Custom modules** should use `/custom/module/collection/data` instead.
- **Export max:** 5000 records per export request.

## Timestamps
All timestamp fields are **epoch seconds** (integer). A value of `0` means "not set".

Legacy product management endpoint (`/product/manage_product`).
Action-based CRUD, Stripe product/price sync, batch retrieval, and export.

ActionQuery.name: action
ActionQuery.description:
Action to perform. Required, with no default: send `action=get` to list records.
A request without it is refused with `{"result": 2, "error": "unsupported_action"}`
over HTTP 200.

PageSizeQuery.name: page_size
PageSizeQuery.description: Number of records per page. Export is capped at 5000.

GetCountQuery.name: get_count
GetCountQuery.description: If true, return only the count without data

SortDictQuery.name: sort_dict
SortDictQuery.description: JSON-encoded sort object. Example: `{"_id": -1}` for descending by creation time.

MatchFilterDictQuery.name: match_filter_dict
MatchFilterDictQuery.description:
JSON-encoded filter object. Example: `{"lead_status": "qualified"}`.
Keys are automatically normalized (e.g. `created_ts` → `timestamp`).
A filter with `$where`, `$function` or `$accumulator` at any depth is
refused with `INVALID_DATA`.

SearchTextQuery.name: search_text
SearchTextQuery.description: Full-text search across entity searchable fields

TenantScopeQuery.name: tenant_scope
TenantScopeQuery.description:
Set to `"true"` to bypass the userid access filter.
- **Tenant admins:** allowed for all actions.
- **Non-admin users:** allowed only for `action=picklist`.
- **Entities without userid:** auto-enabled regardless.

UseNativeQuery.name: use_native
UseNativeQuery.description:
Controls serialization format.
- `true` (default): uses `to_native_response()` with entity-specific collection key.
- `false`: uses `toJSON()` with generic `"values"` collection key.

EntityType.description: Supported entity type identifier, from `_supported_entities` in MdReqHandler. `vendor` is an alias for `account` with `relationship_type` pinned. Note: the type for tasks is `task`. This enum previously said `user_task`, which the API refuses.

PatchableEntityType.description: Entity types that support PATCH updates

NativeListResponse.description:
Response when `use_native=true` (default). The collection key is entity-specific:
`lead_contacts`, `account_contacts`, `accounts`, `opportunities`, `order`,
`invoice`, `product`, `marketing_sources`, `custom_status`, `tasks`, `folders`, `files`, `bill`.

data.description:
Contains the entity-specific collection key (e.g. `lead_contacts`, `accounts`)
and `total_count`.

gross_count.description: Total matching records across all pages (only set on first page)

LegacyListResponse.description: Response when `use_native=false`. Collection key is always `"values"`.

values.description: Array of entity records serialized via toJSON()

export_url.description: URL to download the exported file

data.description: Aggregation results grouped by the requested fields

user_email_not_synced.description: Lead or contact only, when not empty: record id to the code that stopped its registered user's email change (`EMAIL_EMPTY`, `EMAIL_INVALID`, `EMAIL_IN_USE`, `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONFIRMATION_RATE_LIMITED`).

user_email_pending_confirmation.description: Lead or contact only, when not empty. Records whose registered user was sent a code to confirm the new email.

user_phone_not_synced.description: Lead or contact only, when not empty: record id to the code that stopped its registered user's phone change (`PHONE_EMPTY`, `PHONE_INVALID`, `PHONE_IN_USE`, `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONFIRMATION_RATE_LIMITED`).

user_phone_pending_confirmation.description: Lead or contact only, when not empty. Records whose registered user was sent a code to confirm the new number.

data.description: List of deletion results per ID

get.summary: Query entity records with pagination, filtering, and sorting
get.description:
The primary read endpoint for all entity types. Returns paginated records
with optional filtering, sorting, and full-text search.

### Default Behavior
- `action` defaults to `"get"` if not specified
- `use_native` defaults to `true` — records use `to_native_response()` serialization
- Access is filtered by the current user's userid and role hierarchy
- First page (`page_num=1`) also returns `gross_count` with the total matching records

### Collection Key
The key containing the record array in `data` depends on `use_native`:
- **`true`**: entity-specific key (e.g. `data.lead_contacts`, `data.accounts`)
- **`false`**: always `data.values`

parameters.name: entity_id
parameters.description: Fetch a single record by its ID

post.summary: Batch retrieve records by entity IDs or upsert status values
post.description:
POST supports two actions:

### action=get_entity_ids
Retrieve specific records by an array of MongoDB ObjectId strings.
Preferred over GET when you have many IDs or complex filters (avoids URL length limits).

**Serialization:** Respects `use_native` (default `true`).
- `true`: returns records via `to_native_response()` with entity-specific key
- `false`: returns records via `toJSON()` with `"values"` key

**Access control:** Currently queries by `tenant_id` only.
The `tenant_scope` parameter is documented but the POST `get_entity_ids`
path does **not** enforce userid filtering — any authenticated tenant user
can retrieve any record by ID within their tenant.

**Export:** Include `export_settings` to generate a downloadable file instead of inline data.

### action=upsert
Only for `entity_type: "user_status_values"`. Upserts a status value record
matched by tenant_id + value.

entity_ids.description: Required for `get_entity_ids`. Array of MongoDB ObjectId strings.

match_filter_dict.description: Additional MongoDB filter criteria (does not override `_id` or `tenant_id`)

use_native.description:
Controls serialization.
- `true` (default): `to_native_response()` with entity-specific key
- `false`: `toJSON()` with `"values"` key

tenant_scope.description: Set to true to bypass userid filter (tenant admins only)

export_settings.description: Triggers file export instead of inline data

payload.description: Required for `action=upsert`. The record to upsert.

get_entity_ids_export_csv.summary: Batch retrieve and export to CSV

get_entity_ids_export_json.summary: Batch retrieve and export to JSON

patch.summary: Bulk update multiple records or partial update a single record
patch.description:
Supports two modes determined by the `action` field.
The primary use case is **bulk updates** across multiple records.

### Mode 1: Bulk update (`action=bulk_update`) — Primary Use Case
Updates multiple records with the same `$set` payload, in the caller's tenant only.
Supported entity types: `lead`, `contact`, `account`, `opportunity`, `order`,
`invoice`, `product` (anything else is `UNSUPPORTED_ENTITY_TYPE`). The caller needs
`U` on that module (`PRIVILEGE_REQUIRED`). A payload key starting with `$`, or naming
`tenant_id`, `registered_userid`, `linked_contact_id` or `linked_lead_id`, refuses the
call with `FIELD_NOT_EDITABLE` and `fields: [...]`.

This is the recommended way to apply the same field changes across
a batch of records — e.g., tagging, status changes, or assigning owners.

### Mode 2: Single-record partial update (default, no action specified)
Updates a single entity record. Only the provided fields are modified.
For `custom_form_dict`, values are **deep-merged** — existing keys not in
the payload are preserved.

**Supported entity types:** lead, contact, account, opportunity, order, invoice, product

**Entity ID resolution** (first non-empty wins):
1. `entity_id` (top-level)
2. `id` (top-level)
3. `payload.id` or `payload._id`
4. `<entity_type>_id` (top-level or in payload, e.g. `lead_id`)

**Path-based custom attribute updates:**
You can use dot-notation keys like `custom_form_dict.foo` or
`custom_form_dict.nested.key` in the payload. These are automatically
folded into `payload.custom_form_dict` before the deep merge.

### A lead or contact linked to a sign-in account
A lead or contact with `registered_userid` belongs to a user. Its email (the first
`email_list` entry) and phone (the first `phone_list` number) never reach the user
directly. When an update changes either, the record is saved and the user is asked to
confirm the new address or number with a code, as `POST /user/contact/change` would.
The answer says what happened:

- **Single record:** `data` carries `user_email_pending_confirmation: true` or
  `user_email_not_synced: "<code>"`, and `user_phone_pending_confirmation: true` or
  `user_phone_not_synced: "<code>"`, as on `/user/contact` and `/user/lead` `update`.
- **Bulk:** the top level carries `user_email_not_synced: {record id: code}`,
  `user_email_pending_confirmation: [record ids]`, `user_phone_not_synced: {record id:
  code}` and `user_phone_pending_confirmation: [record ids]`, each only when not empty.

Email codes: `EMAIL_EMPTY`, `EMAIL_INVALID`, `EMAIL_IN_USE`, `CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`,
`CONFIRMATION_RATE_LIMITED`. Phone codes: `PHONE_EMPTY`, `PHONE_INVALID`, `PHONE_IN_USE`,
`CONFIRMATION_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONFIRMATION_RATE_LIMITED`. With a `_not_synced` code nothing
was started and the user keeps the old value. The link fields are never a client's.

action.description: Omit for single-record update. Set to `"bulk_update"` for bulk.

entity_ids.description: Required for `bulk_update`. Array of record IDs to update.

payload.description:
Fields to update. For single-record mode, `custom_form_dict` is deep-merged.
For bulk update, applied as `$set` on all matching records.
`_id` in payload is always ignored.

set_contact_status.description: For opportunity updates only — optionally set the linked contact's status

data.description: Per-entity service response (varies by entity type)

delete.summary: Delete entity records by ID or in bulk
delete.description:
Supports deletion of entity records in two modes:

### Service-based entities
`lead`, `contact`, `account`, `opportunity`, `order`, `invoice`, `product`

Uses the appropriate `manage_*` service method which handles cascading
deletes on related entities (activities, comments, attachments).

### Direct entities
`user_status_values`, `custom_status`

Uses direct database operations (no cascading).

### Special action: reset
Bulk-erases **all** records for the specified entity types within the tenant.
Defaults to `dry_run: true` so callers can preview counts before committing.

**Standard entity types** (resolved via `entity_class_dict`, main DB):
`lead`, `contact`, `account`, `opportunity`, `order`, `invoice`, `product`,
`marketing_source`, `custom_status`, `user_task`, `folder`, `file`,
`plaid_item`, `bill`, `payment`, `automation_rules`, `contracts`

**Direct collection types** (main DB, no entity class mapping):
`contract_templates`, `automation_rules_execution_log`

**Custom types** (separate handling):
- `custom_modules` — deletes module definitions from `custom_modules` collection (main DB)
- `custom_objects` — drops custom object data collections from custom DB and
  deletes their metadata from `collection_metadata` (custom DB)

**NOT deleted (left untouched):**
- Customization records (custom fields, picklists, `tenant_form_customization`)
- User accounts and `user_roles`
- `personalization`, `hours_of_operation`, `work_queue`
- Messages, notes, communication records, workflows

**Restrictions:**
- Blocked for tenants `ambivo.com` and `nashapartments.com`
- Requires tenant admin role

**Idempotent:** Yes — uses `delete_many` per entity; returns `deleted_count: 0`
on empty collections. Each entity is processed independently with try/except,
so partial failures do not block remaining entities. Safe to call repeatedly.

### ID resolution
The endpoint checks for IDs in this order:
1. `ids_list` — array of IDs for bulk delete
2. `_id` — single record ID
3. `<entity_type>_id` — entity-specific ID field

ids_list.description: Array of record IDs to delete

entity_list.description: Entity types to reset. Only used when `action=reset`. Includes standard entities, direct collections, and special types (custom_modules, custom_objects).

dry_run.description: When `true` (the default), returns the count of records that *would* be deleted without actually deleting them. Set to `false` to perform the actual deletion. Only used when `action=reset`.

get.summary: Export entity records to CSV, JSON, or Airtable
get.description:
Exports matching records to a downloadable file. Max **5000 records** per request.

### Export Formats
- **CSV**: Default. Returns a URL to a generated CSV file.
- **JSON**: Returns a URL to a generated JSON file.
- **Airtable**: Pushes records to an Airtable base (async, no download URL).

### Serialization
Export always uses `toJSONExport()` with foreign key resolution
(regardless of `use_native`). The response data array is empty —
the file URL is in `export_url`.

### Access Control
Same as `action=get`. Use `tenant_scope=true` (admin only) to export all tenant records.

parameters.name: export_settings
parameters.description:
JSON-encoded export config. Default: `{"export_to": "csv"}`.
For Airtable: `{"export_to": "airtable", "airtable_key": "...", "base_id": "...", "table_name": "..."}`.

get.summary: Fetch records formatted for dropdown / selection components
get.description:
Returns records optimized for UI dropdown/selection components.

### Key Behaviors
- **page_size** is overridden to **1000** for broad coverage
- **Non-admin users CAN use `tenant_scope=true`** — this is the only action
  where non-admins are allowed to bypass the userid filter
- Inventory and procurement types are read through their own service:
  module `R` is required, `tenant_scope` is ignored, `page_size` defaults
  to 1000 and is at most 1000. See "Inventory and procurement picklists".
- Fixed lists (`inventory_uom`, `inventory_item_type`, `inventory_txn_type`,
  `inventory_txn_source_type`, `inventory_txn_reason`, `site`) answer from
  a fixed list. See "Fixed-list picklists"
- When `use_native=false`: uses `toJSONExport()` with `include_id=True`,
  and applies foreign key resolution
- When `use_native=true`: uses `to_native_response()` as normal

get.summary: Retrieve records by an array of entity IDs (GET)
get.description:
Retrieves records by an array of entity IDs passed as a query parameter.
For large ID lists, prefer the POST variant to avoid URL length limits.

### Serialization
The GET variant **always uses `toJSON()`** and returns data under the `"values"` key.
It does **not** respect the `use_native` parameter (unlike the POST variant).

### Export
Pass `export_to=csv` or `export_to=json` to generate a downloadable file.
When exporting, foreign key resolution is applied.

parameters.name: entity_ids
parameters.description: JSON-encoded array of entity ID strings

parameters.name: export_to
parameters.description: Triggers export to CSV or JSON file

get.summary: Group-by aggregation for charts and reports
get.description:
Performs group-by aggregation queries for charting and reporting.
Use `action=chart_config` first to discover valid groupable and aggregate fields.

### Validation
- `group_by_fields` are validated against the entity's chart config
- `aggregate_field` is validated if provided
- Invalid fields return an error with details

### Notes
- `use_native` does **not** apply — returns raw aggregation pipeline output
- Supports nested field grouping (v2 config)
- Default sort: `{"count": -1}` (most frequent first)

post.summary: Action-based product management (CRUD, Stripe sync, batch retrieval, export)
post.description:
The primary product endpoint. All operations are dispatched via the `action` field
in the JSON request body.

**Also mounted at:** `/product` (same handler)

### Supported Actions

| Action | Purpose | Required Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `get` | Get product by ID or paginated list | `product_id` (single) or none (list) |
| `add` | Create a new product | `payload` |
| `update` | Update a product | `product_id`, `payload` |
| `delete` | Delete a product (admin only) | `product_id` |
| `delete_many` | Delete multiple products | `ids_list` |
| `export` | Export products to CSV/JSON | (optional `match_filter_dict`, `export_settings`) |
| `get_entity_ids` | Batch retrieve by entity IDs | `entity_ids` |
| `sync_stripe` | Sync product to Stripe | `payload` |
| `stripe_add` | Create product in Stripe | `product_id` |
| `stripe_update` | Update product in Stripe | `product_id`, `payload` |
| `stripe_delete` | Delete product from Stripe | `product_id` |
| `stripe_price_add` / `add_price` | Add a Stripe price | `product_id`, `payload.price_dict_list` |
| `stripe_price_update` / `update_price` | Update a Stripe price | `product_id`, `payload` (with `stripe_price_id`) |
| `stripe_price_retrieve` | Retrieve a Stripe price | `product_id`, `payload` (with `stripe_price_id`) |
| `stripe_price_delete` | Delete a Stripe price | `product_id`, `payload` (with `stripe_price_id`) |
| `stripe_price_delete_all` | Delete all prices for product | `product_id` |
| `stripe_price_get` | Get price(s) for a product | `product_id` |

### `get_entity_ids` (Batch Retrieval)
Retrieve specific product records by an array of MongoDB ObjectId strings.

**Features:**
- Offset-based pagination (`page_size`, `page_num`)
- Sort control (`sort_dict`)
- Additional filtering (`match_filter_dict`)
- Count-only mode (`get_count`)
- Export to CSV/JSON (`export_settings`)
- Access control bypass (`tenant_scope`)

**Access control:**
- Default: filters by current user's `userid`
- `tenant_scope: true`: bypasses userid filter (any authenticated tenant user)

### `add` with Prices
When creating a product with `action=add`, you can include a `price_dict_list`
at the top level of the request body to create Stripe prices in the same call.

product_id.description: Product ID. Required for get (single), update, delete, and all Stripe operations.

payload.description:
Data payload. Required for `add`, `update`, `sync_stripe`, and Stripe price operations.
For price operations, include `stripe_price_id` to identify the price.

entity_ids.description: Required for `get_entity_ids`. Array of MongoDB ObjectId strings.

ids_list.description: Required for `delete_many`. Array of product IDs to delete.

price_dict_list.description:
Optional for `action=add`. Array of price definitions to create
alongside the new product. Each entry becomes a Stripe price.

last_id.description: Cursor for `get` action — fetch records before this ObjectId

get_count.description: If true, return only the count (for `get_entity_ids`)

match_filter_dict.description:
Additional MongoDB filter criteria. Applied to `get`, `export`, and `get_entity_ids`.
`_id` and `tenant_id` keys are protected and cannot be overridden.

eval_object_id.description: When `"true"`, ObjectId strings in `match_filter_dict` are converted to ObjectId instances

tenant_scope.description:
For `get_entity_ids`: set to `"true"` to bypass the userid filter.
Any authenticated tenant user can use this — entity IDs serve as access control.

export_settings.description: For `export` and `get_entity_ids`. Triggers file export instead of inline data.

is_debug.description: Enable debug mode for service operations

get.summary: Query products with pagination, filtering, or batch retrieve by IDs
get.description:
GET endpoint for product retrieval. Supports two modes based on the `action` parameter.

### action=get (default)
Standard paginated product query with filtering, sorting, and search.

**Access control:**
- Default: filtered by current user's `userid` + role hierarchy
- `tenant_scope=true`:
  - **Tenant admins:** bypasses userid filter for all actions
  - **Non-admin users:** allowed only for `action=picklist`

### action=get_entity_ids
Retrieve specific products by an array of entity IDs.

**Serialization:** Always returns `toJSON()` format under the `"values"` key.

**Features:**
- Offset-based pagination (`page_size`, `page_num`)
- Sort control (`sort_dict`)
- Additional filtering (`match_filter_dict`)
- Count-only mode (`get_count`)
- Export to CSV/JSON (`export_to`)
- Access control bypass (`tenant_scope`)

### action=picklist
Same as `get` but non-admin users can use `tenant_scope=true`
to access all tenant products (for populating dropdowns).

- `action=get_entity_ids`: any authenticated tenant user (IDs serve as access control)
- `action=picklist`: any authenticated user (for dropdown population)
- `action=get`: tenant admins only

patch.summary: Partial update a product with deep merge on custom_form_dict
patch.description:
Updates a single product record. Only the provided fields are modified.
For `custom_form_dict`, values are **deep-merged** — existing keys not in
the payload are preserved.

**Path-based custom attribute updates:**
You can use dot-notation keys like `custom_form_dict.foo` in the payload.
These are automatically folded into `payload.custom_form_dict` before the deep merge.

**Entity ID resolution** (first non-empty wins):
1. `product_id` (top-level)
2. `id` (top-level)

**Intuit sync:** If `payload.source_id` is set and `payload.data_source` is `"intuit"`,
the record is timestamped with `interface_ts` and linked to the tenant's Intuit realm.

payload.description:
Fields to update. `custom_form_dict` is deep-merged with existing values.
Supports dot-notation keys (e.g. `custom_form_dict.foo`).

delete.description:
Deletes one or more product records via `ProductService.manage_product`.

**ID resolution:**
1. `product_id` — single product delete (`action=delete`)
2. `ids_list` — bulk delete (`action=delete_many`)
